beliefs.practice: Read the DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any DB credentials) from environment variables at runtime and never commit secrets into the repo; provide a .env.example placeholder instead.

Create and reuse a single MongoClient connection (one instance per Node.js process) rather than opening a new connection per request; configure connection pool size (maxPoolSize) and timeouts at startup.
Enable TLS/SSL for the connection and validate server certificates; never disable certificate validation in production.
Implement exponential-backoff retries for transient errors and specifically handle 429 (throttling / rate limit) responses and network timeouts; surface/fail after a bounded number of retries.

Provision and monitor throughput (RUs) for the database/collections and design queries to minimize RU cost: use projections to fetch only needed fields and avoid returning large documents unnecessarily.

Choose an appropriate partition key for collections (e.g., applicationId or customerId) to avoid hot partitions and cross-partition fan-out; design queries to be targeted to a single partition where possible.
Create indexes on frequently filtered/sorted fields used by the pipeline (e.g., applicationId, status, createdAt, applicant.ssn or normalized email) so lookups and sorts are covered by the index.
Avoid unindexed queries and full-collection scans in production; use explain() during development to verify queries use indexes and examine their RU/IO cost.

For vector similarity search, create a dedicated vector index on the embedding field with parameters tuned to the embedding dimension (e.g., HNSW/IVF parameters appropriate for your vector length); keep embeddings as dense numeric arrays in a single field.
When performing ANN/vector queries, limit candidate sizes and fetch only required document fields (projection) before post-filtering/deduplication to control RU and memory usage.
Use idempotent writes for pipeline output (upsert by applicationId or decisionId) so repeated/failed retries do not create duplicates; seed scripts should be idempotent (check and upsert).

Limit document size to the platform maximum and avoid embedding very large blobs; if storing large text or binary (attachments), use external storage (e.g., Blob Storage) and store references in DocumentDB.
Use TTL (time-to-live) indexes for ephemeral or cache-like collections (e.g., temporary embeddings, intermediate pipeline artifacts) to automatically purge old data and save storage/RUs.

Perform input validation and sanitize any free-text fields before passing them to the LLM layer or using them in DB queries; avoid storing PII unless necessary and encrypt sensitive fields at rest or in application layer.

Use least-privilege credentials for the app — create a DB user with only required privileges (read on applications, write on decisions) rather than using a full admin key; rotate credentials regularly.
Design queries and indexes to avoid cross-partition sorts and aggregations; where heavy aggregation is required, consider pre-aggregating or using targeted partition queries.
Close the MongoClient cleanly on application shutdown and ensure background pipeline tasks are drained before exit to avoid leaked connections or partial writes.
Instrument and monitor query latency, RU consumption, throttling (429s), connection pool metrics and errors using Azure Monitor / Application Insights and add alerts for high throttling or errors.
Mock the DB and LLM in unit tests (as you did) and reserve live-cluster integration tests for CI or gated tests that explicitly use the DOCUMENTDB_URI; keep unit tests hermetic.

Avoid long-running multi-document transactions across different partitions; prefer idempotent single-document updates or orchestrated workflows with compensation logic if multi-collection atomicity is required.

Use projections to limit returned fields (e.g., exclude large embedding vectors when not needed) and paginate results rather than relying on skip for deep offsets; prefer range-based pagination by indexed timestamp or _id.
When storing embeddings, persist metadata used by agents (source doc id, chunk id, text snippet) as separate indexed fields to allow efficient retrieval after a vector hit.
